questions.question:
Read this email from your English-speaking friend Tom and the notes you have made.

From: Tom
Subject: Our cooking evening

Hi!
I’m really looking forward to the cooking evening we’re organising for our class next Friday. [Note 1: Me too!] About twelve people are coming. Should we cook one big meal together or ask everyone to bring a dish? [Note 2: Say which and why] I can bring plates and glasses from my house. What else do we need? [Note 3: Tell Tom] Also, my cousin Ellie is staying with us that weekend. Is it all right if she comes too? [Note 4: Yes, because …]

Cheers,
Tom

Write your email to Tom using all the notes. Write about 100 words.
questions.explanation:
A good answer replies to all four notes: (1) says you are also looking forward to the evening; (2) chooses between cooking one big meal and asking everyone to bring a dish, and gives a reason; (3) tells Tom what else you need, for example food, drinks or kitchen things; (4) agrees that Ellie can come and says why. Use an informal greeting and ending, link your ideas and write about 100 words.

Model answer:
Hi Tom,
Me too – I can’t wait! It’s going to be great fun.
I think we should cook one big meal together, like a pasta dish. That way everyone can help in the kitchen, and it’s cheaper than buying lots of different things.
Thanks for the plates and glasses. We’ll also need some big pans, a few sharp knives and something to drink. I can get the vegetables from the market on Thursday.
Of course Ellie can come! The more people we have, the better, and she can meet everyone in our class.
See you on Friday,
Maria

questions.question:
Choose ONE of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

Question 2 – Article
You see this announcement on an English-language website for teenagers.

Articles wanted!
MY FAVOURITE MEAL
What is your favourite meal? Who makes it, and when do you usually eat it? Why do you like it so much?
Write an article answering these questions. The best articles will appear on our website next month.

Write your article.

Question 3 – Story
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
Suddenly there was smoke everywhere in the kitchen.

Write your story.
questions.explanation:
Article: give your article a title, answer every question in the announcement (the meal, who makes it and when, why you like it) and make it interesting for the reader, for example by describing the taste or a special memory. Story: begin with the given sentence, use past tenses, and give the story a clear development and ending. In both tasks write about 100 words.

Model article:
Granny’s Sunday soup
My favourite meal is a vegetable soup that my grandmother makes. We eat it every Sunday when the whole family visits her flat.
She puts in carrots, potatoes, beans and lots of herbs from her small garden, and she always serves it with warm bread that she bakes herself. It smells wonderful as soon as you open the door!
Why do I love it so much? Partly because it tastes delicious, but mostly because it reminds me of happy afternoons with my cousins, talking and laughing around her little kitchen table.

Model story:
Suddenly there was smoke everywhere in the kitchen. I had wanted to surprise my parents with a special breakfast, but I had forgotten about the toast while I was making the eggs.
I opened all the windows and threw the black bread into the bin. Just then the smoke alarm started ringing loudly, and my dad ran downstairs in his pyjamas.
“What’s happening?” he shouted. When he saw the plates on the table, he started to smile.
In the end we ate eggs without toast, and Dad said it was the best breakfast he had ever had.
